title: A tile equals its report straight after new data is added
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Revenue tile and choose This Week. Revenue must read $0.00 with 0 Invoices under it. If it shows anything else, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Create a test customer: Customers > New Customer, name it (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1") and save. On its Contacts tab add a contact (e.g. "Dana Test"). On its Assets tab add an asset (e.g. unit "ZZ-101") and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  6. Have a technician who works at this location and can clock time (e.g. "Tom Tech"): Settings > Staff > open the technician and check the Time Clock setting is on. You need this technician's sign-in to clock time in a second browser or a private window.
  7. Have a department for internal work with the time clock on: Settings > Departments (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Shop Cleanup").
  8. Prepare (do not invoice yet) one work order for the test customer: Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create. Set Service Advisor and mileage, add one line (Estimated Time 2.50 at e.g. $100.00 per hour, Tech Time 2.50, Approved), type a Story, set the line Complete, Complete Work Order, Mark Reviewed.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week and write down the figure ($0.00).
  2. Open the work order, Finance tab > Create Invoice, and close the payment dialog without paying (subtotal e.g. $250.00).
  3. At once click Dashboard (or reload the page), set Revenue to This Week and write down the figure.
  4. At once open Reports > Sales (Date: This week) and write down the Totals row Subtotal.
  5. Reverse the invoice: open the work order, Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm.
  6. At once read Revenue (This Week) on the Dashboard and the Sales report total again.
  7. In the second browser, signed in as Tom Tech, click Clock In in the top menu, choose the department, wait about 6 minutes, and clock out.
  8. At once read Technician Utilization (This Week) on the Dashboard and the Summary row of the Technician Utilization report (Date: This week).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Straight after the invoice, Revenue reads $250.00 and the Sales report reads $250.00. You never need to wait for the tile to catch up.
  • Straight after the reversal, both read $0.00.
  • Straight after the clock-out, Technician Utilization and its report both show the new internal time (0.00% with 0.00 WO Hrs and about 0.10 Clocked), matching each other.
  • At no reading does the tile show an older figure than its report. Whether the dashboard's stored figures are cleared at the right moment inside the system cannot be checked by hand: write "internal refresh not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you see.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R1, S3-N1). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After, 10_sales_After, 13_technician-utilization_After.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3-N1: “If a measure's report shows a value, the matching tile shows the same value; the two never disagree.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
